title: D150 v1: scheduled_species_turnover@1's clearance with resolved_pump_tissue@3's face law in resolved_pump_composite@1, against the exact discrete solution and the held sphere's continuum closed forms
status: PROPOSED (drafted 14 November 2026 from the development runs named beside its numbers and revised the same day after the lead's review with the advisor; not registered, and no judged run is made before the lead registers it)
scope: the lead's review: the judged arms run resolved_pump_tissue@3's faces with exact radial conductances (4 pi r_a r_b over r_b - r_a between the points each face joins) and scheduled_species_turnover@1's first-order clearance at every shell, with a held-bath source (the source bath at c0) and an outer bath at the trace, in resolved_pump_composite@1. scheduled_species_exchange@1, turnover's production and the occupant rule enter only through Q5's guard test files. This is design §6's first acceptance (the held sphere with decay, the finite-domain steady state, the exact finite-volume solution), so no arm is missing; a qualified statement from this protocol carries this scope

references.R-discrete: validation/tissue/secreted_species_radial.py solution: each arm's own declared finite-volume system (the same faces, volumes, clearance and baths), solved exactly by the matrix exponential
references.R-continuum: validation/tissue/secreted_species_closed_forms.py HeldSphere: the finite-domain solution of the held sphere with first-order decay through v = r u, its steady state plus a finite sum of sine modes, every quantity an exact integral (the shells' averages, the amount, the two baths' supplies and the clearance); tests/unit/test_secreted_species_closed_forms.py checks it against the PDE itself without the builder (the residual of u_t = D lap u - k u by fourth-order differences, both boundary conditions over time, the start and the steady state against their sinh forms), against quadrature and against its own mass balance
references.independence: both NumPy, written from the design's Appendix A, never from engine code; neither takes measured data or fits anything (D151)
references.common_mode: R-discrete shares the builder's declared system, so a builder error would be common-mode in Q1; Q2 against R-continuum covers it, as its planar control shows (the lead's review)

world.start: the steady state plus two positive sine modes of v (index, amplitude in mM m): [[1, 5e-09], [2, 2.0000000000000005e-09]]; each shell starts at its exact average
world.faces: each face declared with the exact spherical-shell conductance between the points it joins, area 4 pi r_a r_b over length r_b - r_a (the lead's requirement on radial builders, §11.5 item 8)
world.regime: kt 0.25 to 4 at the records, R / lambda = 0.5, the medium out to 6 lambda: the first calibration target's non-dimensional regime (kt below 1, profiles over a few lambda; §6), compressed in time (k = 1/s; §4.5)
world.ions: quiescent: no pump or channel, zero membrane permeability and zero ion face diffusivity (the species-only world)
disclosures: dr1.25_dt0.5 runs at dt K_ii 0.384, beyond the probed 0.30; it passed every host check in development and carries Q2's spatial term and Q3's spatial order (accepted at the lead's review, with this disclosure)

rules.tolerances: every tolerance number is computed from the development run named beside it (validation/tissue/secreted_species_protocol.py draft); development runs are not judged
rules.judged_run: once, after registration, from a fresh clean execution snapshot of main (validation/source_snapshot.py, no dirty patch), through scripts/run_detached.sh. A failure is recorded and diagnosed, never retuned
rules.attempts: an attempt that ends by infrastructure before its verdict is written is not a verdict: an out-of-memory kill, a unit stopped by the slice, a host crash, a harness timeout, a unit killed by its runtime limit (--runtime-max), or a Q5 test file whose process ends by a signal (judge-q5 then writes infrastructure.json, not verdict.json). It is recorded with its logs and partial outputs and rerun once from the same snapshot; each attempt writes its own output directory, since every judge entry refuses an existing one. A second infrastructure ending goes to the lead, as does any other ending without a verdict. A run that has written its verdict is final (S5's rule). An arm the engine refuses is a verdict: its items fail; a test failure or error inside a completed run is a verdict too (pre_registration_amendments)
rules.timing: each judged entry runs through scripts/run_detached.sh with --oom-first in its own unit: the judge with --runtime-max 1400 (about 3 x the rehearsal's 457 s), judge-q5 with --runtime-max 3100 (about 3 x the rehearsal's Q5 total of 1011 s under load, its longest file 439 s) and no per-file cap, combine with --runtime-max 600. The judged units run without --wait-headroom: the lead launches each only after checking that the slice has about 3 GB free for judge and for judge-q5 (the dry runs' peaks 1.8 and 2.1 GB, plus a margin), so each runtime limit measures the entry alone and no wait can spend the single rerun
rules.resolved_start: every judged arm runs through the runner with every host check, from a pre-formed profile (the lead's ruling 5) that meets both boundary conditions at t = 0. A switch-on from the trace is no judged arm: the host energy ledger refuses an unresolved onset (§11.4). A ramped source is inadmissible until a probe measures it
rules.guard_world: the species-only world: the ions quiescent, so the energy bound is the species' own (§7)
rules.guards_of_record: energy: RK4 for the face heat and the operators' work (the radial and face-free worlds, the absolute bound 2e-8 pJ; tests/unit/test_secreted_species_guards.py, test_secreted_species_runs.py), and a NumPy dG test per law (Decimal, 50 digits; tests/unit/test_species_turnover.py, test_species_exchange.py). The IMEX bound is blind to the species' bookings in mixed worlds and coarse in species-only ones, so it is no guard of record (§12.1)

judge_entries.guard: validation/tissue/secreted_species_protocol.registered, the judge's first call: it refuses an unregistered protocol and a source that is not a clean execution snapshot before anything is computed or written; tests/unit/test_secreted_species_judged_refusal.py tests it, with judge_q5 and combine, on edited copies
judge_entries.Q5: python -m validation.tissue.secreted_species_qualification judge-q5 OUT: the same guard, then pytest on Q5's list from the snapshot, one file at a time with no per-file cap; OUT/verdict.json with each file's counts, exit code and duration
judge_entries.combined: python -m validation.tissue.secreted_species_qualification combine OUT Q1_Q2_Q3_OUT Q5_OUT: the same guard; the one qualification verdict (every item, the scope line, the snapshot's revision, the reported step-map ratios), refusing verdicts of another protocol or from another snapshot
judge_entries.existing_out: every entry refuses an existing OUT before anything runs

development_runs.splitting_bias_m2: /mnt/workspaces/Cells/secreted-species-v1-20261114-01/splitting_bias.json (milestone 2: the formula verified against the step map's fixed point)

Q1.claim: The engine's time integration of the declared finite-volume system is bounded a priori by the splitting's leading term (within 3 x it at every record), and lies within 3 x its own step term (S5's dt study): the judged arms (2.5 um; IMEX at 1 ms, RK4 at 0.1 ms) against R-discrete
Q1.what_the_rules_show: the lead's review: the dt-study rule detects bias, not order. For a second-order error against an exact reference, 3 x the halving difference puts the pass fraction near 4/9 (development: 0.468 IMEX, 0.449 RK4); a first-order scheme would give about 2/3 and still pass, so order is Q3's. The splitting-term rule is the one judged bound not scaled from the engine's own runs; it is one-sided, so it bounds the step term and does not identify it. The identification is reported: the step map's fixed point matches the first shell's error to 5.8e-04 (IMEX) and 7.8e-04 (RK4) at the first record, and to 1.9e-07 and 2.0e-04 at the last (relative). The judged controls show that each rule can fail
Q1.dt_study_rule: S5's form, per shell and record: the step term |q(dt) - q(dt/2)| on the same grid; tolerance 3 x the step term, or the floor 64 eps x the scale (the largest concentration over the arm's records, the engine's at the judged step) where that is larger
Q1.splitting_term_rule: the lead's milestone-3 instruction, per record in the max norm over shells: the step term dt^2 k (g - k c_ss) / 4 under ARS(2,2,2) and / 12 under RK4 (§12.1), with g the source face's kappa c0 / V0 and c_ss the declared system's steady state, at the first shell, which carries the error; tolerance 3 x (|term| + the floor). The term is the leading order of the composite step's steady bias: the split scheme's first shell runs low by it
Q1.verdict_rule: pass when, for both arms, both rules hold at every record and both rules catch their registered controls for k and for D
Q1.predictions: reported, not judged: the step map's exact fixed point (the steady bias in full) and the step map iterated in NumPy (ARS's explicit stages or RK4's polynomial, the clearance's exact half-steps around them), whose distance from R-discrete predicts the engine's error at every shell and record. The map's agreement with the engine is a tier-2 regression guard (regression_guards), not a judged item: one author wrote both sides
Q1.controls: judged (the lead's review, S5's form): the judged arm's output against R-discrete with the clearance, and separately the diffusivity, x (1 + delta), at each rule's and arm's registered delta: 10 x the larger of the smallest deltas that rule caught for k and for D in development (a 1-2-5 grid from 1e-14 to 0.5; where, as [record, shell] or [record]). Each rule must catch both: its measure exceeds its tolerance somewhere

Q2.claim: The engine solves the held sphere with first-order decay to its spatial and temporal step terms: the judged IMEX arm (2.5 um, 1 ms) against R-continuum

quantities_described.coarse: each 5 um shell's average (24), aggregated exactly from the grid's shells (mM)
quantities_described.outer_supplied_fmol: the outer bath's cumulative supply (negative: it absorbs)

Q2.spatial_step_term_rule: |q(2.5 um) - q(1.25 um)| at 0.5 ms, per element and record
Q2.time_step_term_rule: |q(1 ms) - q(0.5 ms)| at 2.5 um, per element and record
Q2.reference_term_rule: 64 eps x the quantity's scale (the closed form is exact)
Q2.tolerance_rule: 3 x (spatial + time + reference) per element and record
Q2.verdict_rule: pass when every element's |engine - R-continuum| is within its tolerance and the planar control fails every quantity's
Q2.what_the_rule_shows: as with Q1's dt study, a pass fraction near 4/9 is structural for second-order errors (development: 0.44 to 0.47), so the tolerance's power is its judged control's: the probes' planar faces exceed it 28 to 248 times in development
Q2.control: judged (the lead's review): the planar-face arm (planar_dr2.5_dt1: the probes' faces, area 4 pi r^2 at the edge, otherwise the judged arm) against R-continuum must fail every quantity's tolerance (its largest fraction above 1)

Q3.claim: The observed orders are about 2 in space and in time
Q3.reported_not_banded: the observed orders are reported (S3's and S5's registered form); only the stop rules are judged
Q3.difference: per quantity and record, the largest |q(h) - q(h/2)| over the quantity's elements (the shells or the 24 coarse shells; a scalar is its own)
Q3.measurable: a quantity at a record whose two successive differences both lie above 64 eps x its scale (the largest |value| over every element, record and arm), defined before the judged run
stop_rules: every measurable difference decreases from the (5, 2.5 um) pair to the (2.5, 1.25 um) pair, at 0.5 ms (the coarse shells and the four scalars)
every measurable difference decreases from the (1, 0.5 ms) pair to the (0.5, 0.25 ms) pair, at 2.5 um (the shells and the four scalars)
a quantity that does not converge stops the run for a report
Q3.why_the_max_norm: a development finding: element by element (S5's Q5 wording, written for scalar components), one of the 120 coarse-shell differences in space does not fall: coarse shell 19 at 2 s, where the spatial error changes sign (-9.6e-9 to +1.6e-8 of c0 across shells 18 and 19). There the difference's leading term vanishes and the next need not fall (its first difference is 1.2e-6 of that record's largest), while the element's errors against R-continuum fall (2.2e-11, 1.6e-11, 4.6e-12 mM). A monotonicity test per element of a sign-changing field is ill-posed at the crossing, so the rule takes the max norm; the per-element count is reported (development, per_element_reported). Q1's and Q2's tolerances stay per element: a magnitude bound is not ill-posed there, and every element passes
Q3.why_differences: an error against R-continuum can change sign between grids: the clearance's at 0.25 s does from 5 to 2.5 um, so it grows there while the differences decrease. The errors' orders against R-continuum are reported beside the stop rules

Q4.claim: The switch-on against the Danckwerts form near the source
Q4.reason: reported only, under the resolved-start rule (rules.resolved_start; the lead's ruling 5, confirmed at the lead's review): a switch-on cannot pass the host energy ledger (§11.4), so it would run through the checked step map without the runner's host checks, and the infinite-medium form differs from the finite domain's at the outer bath
Q4.record: probe 4 (§11.3 (b)): through the checked step map, 2.5 um, 1 ms, 2,000 steps, no step refused; 8.6e-7 to 4.2e-9 of c0 from the exact discrete solution at 0.25 to 2 s, and its gap from the Danckwerts form approaches the smooth start's
